# @forgesworn/qr

> QR code encoder and decoder with no dependencies, for browsers, workers and Node. Versions 1-40, levels L/M/Q/H, numeric, alphanumeric and byte modes, optional UTF-8 ECI, SVG, canvas and terminal output. The decoder reads RGBA or greyscale camera frames, including rotated, tilted, mirrored and inverted codes. Tests compare 114 symbols module for module with ZXing, read output back with jsQR, and require the decoder to read at least as many synthetic distorted frames as jsQR.

ESM only, Node.js 22.13+.

## Install

```bash
npm install @forgesworn/qr
```

## API

- `encode(data: string | Uint8Array, options?: EncodeOptions): QrCode` - options `ecc` ('L'|'M'|'Q'|'H', default 'M'), `version` (1-40), `minVersion`, `mask` (0-7), `mode` ('numeric'|'alphanumeric'|'byte'), `eci` (boolean). Throws `QrCapacityError` (a RangeError) when the data does not fit.
- `QrCode` - `{ version, ecc, mask, mode, size, modules }`; `modules` is a row-major Uint8Array, 1 = dark, no quiet zone.
- `isDark(qr, x, y): boolean`
- `toSvg(qr, { margin = 4, dark = '#000', light = '#fff' | null, title? }): string`
- `drawCanvas(canvas, qr, { width = 8 px per module, margin = 4, dark, light | null }): void` - any HTMLCanvasElement or OffscreenCanvas; resizes it to width square.
- `toTerminal(qr, { margin = 4, ink = 'light' | 'dark' }): string` - half-block text; 'light' ink for dark terminal backgrounds.
- `decode(image: { data, width, height }, { rowStride?, channels?: 1 | 4, inversion?: 'normal' | 'inverted' | 'both' }): DecodeResult | undefined` - data is RGBA (ImageData) or greyscale; result `{ text, bytes, version, ecc, mask, eci, corrected, mirrored, inverted, location }`; undefined when no readable code is found.
- `decodeModules(modules, size)` - reads a row-major module grid (no quiet zone), straight or mirrored.

## Example

```ts
import { encode, toSvg } from '@forgesworn/qr'
const svg = toSvg(encode('https://example.com/', { ecc: 'Q' }))

import { decode } from '@forgesworn/qr'
const text = decode(ctx.getImageData(0, 0, w, h))?.text
```
